anomalies.observed: The PCA9685PW PWM driver (U2) is drawn with its address-select pins A0–A5 (pins 1–6) pulled to a fixed level and the sheet annotation under the block reads 'I2C address: 0x41', placing the device on the FCC I2C2 bus at 0x41.
anomalies.expected: The design specification lists the PWM/servo driver as 'NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40', and the INA219AIDCNR on the same I2C2_SCL_FCC/I2C2_SDA_FCC bus is itself at 0x40 (A0=A1=GND).

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40
PWM Driver ... I2C address: 0x41 (FCC Peripherals sheet)
Voltage/Current/Power Sense IC ... I2C address: 0x40 (Power sheet)

anomalies.impact: The PWM driver answers at a different 7-bit address than the firmware/spec expects, so servo output initialisation and PWM channel writes would fail (or collide with the INA219 if the address pins are actually grounded, giving 0x40 on the same bus as the current sensor).

parsed.summary: The only concrete drawing-vs-spec discrepancy found is the PCA9685 PWM driver's I2C address: the schematic annotates 0x41 while the specification (and the co-resident INA219 on the same I2C2 bus) requires 0x40, a mismatch that would prevent the firmware from talking to the servo driver. Other blocks (power tree, MCU pin-out, sensor set, inter-MCU UART/I2C/GPIO links, known barometer pin-swap bug) match the specification.
